source_text:
Αὕτη ἡ ὁδός, ἀγαπητοί, ἐν ᾖ εὕρομεν τὸ σωτήριον ἡμῶν, Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, τὸν ἀρχιερέα τῶν προσφορῶν ἡμῶν, τὸν προστάτην καὶ βοηθὸν τῆς ἀσθενείας ἡμῶν.
διὰ τούτου ἀτενίζομεν εἰς τὰ ὕψη τῶν οὐρανῶν, διὰ τούτου ἐνοπτριζόμεθα τὴν ἄμωμον καὶ ὑπερτάτην ὄψιν αὐτοῦ, διὰ τούτου ἠνεῴχθησαν ἡμῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ τῆς καρδίας, διὰ τούτου ἡ ἀσύνετος καὶ ἐσκοτωμένη διάνοια ἡμῶν ἀναθάλλει εἰς τὸ φῶς, διὰ τούτου ἠθέλησεν ὁ δεσπότης τῆς ἀθανάτου γνώσεως ἡμᾶς γεύσασθαι, ὃς ὦν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς μεγαλωσύνης αὐτοῦ, τοσούτῳ μείζων ἐστὶν ἀγγέλων, ὅσῳ διαφορώτερον ὄνομα κεκληρονόμηκεν.
γέγραπται γὰρ οὕτως: Ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ πνεύματα καὶ τοὺς λειτουργοὺς αὐτοῦ πυρὸς φλόγα.
ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ οὕτως εἶπεν ὁ δεσπότης. Υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε: αἴτησαι παῤ ἐμοῦ, καὶ δώσω σοι ἔθνη τὴν κληρονομίαν σου καὶ τὴν κατάσχεσίν σου τὰ πέρατα τῆς γῆς.
καὶ πάλιν λέγει πρὸς αὐτόν: Κάθον ἐκ δεξιῶν μου, ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.
τίνες οὖν οἱ ἐχθροί; οἱ φαῦλοι καὶ ἀντιτασσομενοι τῷ θελήματι αὐτοῦ.
thought_title: Christ the Way to the Father's Glory
orientation: The Roman church is addressing the Corinthians, explaining that Jesus Christ is the way through whom they found salvation and through whom God has opened their hearts to light and knowledge.
pass_a_gloss: This is the way, beloved, in which we found our salvation, Jesus Christ, the high priest of our offerings, the protector and helper of our weakness. Through this one we gaze into the heights of the heavens, through this one we see mirrored the blameless and most high face of him, through this one the eyes of our heart were opened, through this one our foolish and darkened understanding blossoms into the light, through this one the master wished us to taste the immortal knowledge, who, being the radiance of his majesty, is so much greater than angels as he has inherited a more excellent name. For it is written thus: He who makes his angels winds and his ministers a flame of fire. But concerning his son the master spoke thus: You are my son, today I have begotten you; ask from me, and I will give you nations as your inheritance and as your possession the ends of the earth. And again he says to him: Sit at my right hand, until I place your enemies as a footstool of your feet. Who then are the enemies? The wicked and those who oppose his will.

choices.why: Keeps the cultic sense of προσφορά as offering, matching the priestly role of Christ in the argument
Both nouns are functional titles; protector captures προστάτης as one who stands before/defends, helper captures βοηθός as one who comes to aid
The middle voice of ἐνοπτρίζομαι means to behold as in a mirror; the rendering keeps the mirror imagery explicit
ἀσύνετος means without understanding or foolish; ἐσκοτωμένη is a perfect passive participle meaning darkened; both adjectives modify διάνοια as the mind or understanding
ἀπαύγασμα is the brightness or radiance that shines forth from a source; μεγαλωσύνη is majesty or greatness, a divine attribute
The genitive πυρός specifies the material of the flame; the phrase is a Hebraism meaning a blazing fire, kept literally

pass_b_english: This is the way, beloved, in which we found our salvation: Jesus Christ, the high priest of our offerings, the protector and helper of our weakness.

Through him we gaze into the heights of the heavens. Through him we see mirrored his spotless and most exalted face. Through him the eyes of our heart were opened. Through him our foolish and darkened understanding blossoms into the light. Through him the Master willed that we taste immortal knowledge. He is the radiance of his majesty, and he is as much greater than the angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent.
For it is written this way: “He makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire” (Psalm 104:4).

But about his Son the Master said this: “You are my Son; today I have begotten you. Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession” (Psalm 2:7-8).
And again he says to him: “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet” (Psalm 110:1).
Who then are the enemies? Those who are wicked and oppose his will.

problems.source_quote: Ὁ ποιῶν τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ πνεύματα
problems.why: πνεύματα means 'spirits' not 'winds'. Hebrew of Psalm 104:4 has 'winds' but LXX has πνεύματα = 'spirits'. The English follows Hebrew rather than LXX source text.
problems.ruling: πνεύματα means 'spirits'; 'winds' follows Hebrew, not the Greek LXX text the source quotes.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by adding a colon after 'salvation' so readers immediately see that Jesus Christ is the way being described. Broke the long second paragraph into shorter sentences to make each 'through him' clause easier to follow aloud. Kept all quotations, references, and claims exactly as in the source.

last_rejected.quote: He is the radiance of his majesty, and he is as much greater than the angels
last_rejected.source_quote: ὃς ὦν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς μεγαλωσύνης αὐτοῦ, τοσούτῳ μείζων ἐστὶν ἀγγέλων
last_rejected.why: The new-sentence “He” takes the Master as subject. The relative refers to Christ, the radiance of God’s majesty, greater than the angels.
last_rejected.fix: Through him the Master willed that we taste immortal knowledge—Christ, the radiance of his majesty, as much greater than the angels as the name he has inherited is more excellent.
last_rejected.ruling: The relative ὃς ὦν ἀπαύγασμα τῆς μεγαλωσύνης αὐτοῦ refers to Christ, and "He is the radiance... greater than the angels" follows from the prior clause about Christ; no change in meaning.
